name: aisync
purpose: one standup for all your AI coding tools: shared rules, a hash-chained journal, file claims and mid-session news for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor

credits.name: AGENTS.md
credits.evidence: The starting idea: one plain-text instruction file every agent reads, no SDK. aisync keeps that shape for shared rules (one rules block copied into each tool's own AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md) and adds what a static file cannot say: who is editing what right now, and what changed since the session started.

credits.name: Claude Code
credits.evidence: Mid-session news rides on Claude Code hooks: `aisync install-hooks` adds SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and PostToolUse entries to ~/.claude/settings.json, and `aisync hook claude-code` answers with hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext only when another tool changed something.

credits.name: Codex
credits.evidence: Codex reads ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, which is where aisync seeds the shared rules block, and its hooks.json takes the same SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit / PostToolUse events, so `aisync hook codex` reuses the Claude Code reply format.

credits.name: Cursor
credits.evidence: Cursor hooks (~/.cursor/hooks.json) deliver the rules and progress at sessionStart and the news after each postToolUse through additional_context, because Cursor's User Rules live inside the app instead of a file aisync could sync.

credits.name: git
credits.evidence: The journal borrows git's hash chain: every event stores the id of the one before it and its own id is a SHA-256 of that link plus its body, so `aisync verify` spots any edited, lost or reordered line. The hub itself is a local git repo.
